# `posture`

How a body holds itself: what that makes of its height, its speed, how it is perceived and what it can use (06 §11.1).

## Fields

Besides these, a definition takes the [keys every definition carries](README.md#keys-every-definition-carries).

- `name` ([text](../values.md#texts), or `null`; optional): What a reader calls it.
- `height` (number; optional): The share of its standing height the body has in this posture. Above zero.
- `speed` (number; optional): A factor on the speed of every way of moving. Zero or more.
- `movement` (list of id of a [`movement`](movement.md); optional): The ways of moving allowed in this posture. Empty for all.
- `signature` (number; optional): A factor on how easily the body is perceived (15 §5.3). Carried for the perception package.
- `occupies` (object, id of a [`channel`](channel.md) → [`Slots`](#slots); optional): The channel slots that cannot be used while in this posture (03 §6.2).
- `traits` (list of string; optional): Traits the posture carries, by id, as written. Carried until traits are joined to postures.
- `look` (string, or `null`; optional): How the body is drawn in it (12 §4.4), as written. Reported with `posture_changed`.

<a id="slots"></a>
### `Slots`

How many slots of one channel are needed (03 §6.2).

In data, a whole number of at least one, or `"all"`.

Written as a number of slots, or "all".

Takes:

- a string
- an integer
